html:
Mukhtar Auezov (1897 to 1961) was a Kazakh writer and scholar, best known for The Path of Abai, an epic novel about the poet Abai Qunanbaiuly. He grew up near Semipalatinsk in Abai's own country; his family had known the poet, and his grandfather, a teller of folk tales, taught him to read.

He wrote plays from the 1910s, among them Enlik-Kebek, a tragedy of lovers from feuding clans. In the 1930s he was arrested and accused of nationalism, and he survived by publicly recanting. The novel, published in parts from 1942 to 1956, follows Abai's life and through it the society of the 19th century steppe: its clans, feuds, seasonal migrations and the coming of Russian rule. It was translated into many languages and won the highest Soviet prizes.

Auezov also studied and defended the Manas epic of the Kyrgyz, and taught at the university in Almaty. His home there is a museum, and the national drama theatre and a university bear his name. He set the path for later writers of the region such as Chinghiz Aitmatov.
